title: Norwegian Wood
author: Haruki Murakami
synopsis: A middle-aged man is pulled back to his student days in 1960s Tokyo by the sound of an old song, and to the two very different women who shaped that time. Murakami trades his usual surrealism for something quieter: grief, memory, and the strange loneliness of being young.
authorBio: Haruki Murakami is a Japanese novelist whose work blends the everyday with the uncanny, earning him a devoted global readership.
staffNote: Read this on a train if you can. Bring tissues. — R.

title: The Kite Runner
author: Khaled Hosseini
synopsis: A boyhood betrayal in Kabul follows Amir across decades and continents, until a phone call offers a way back to the friend he failed. A story about guilt, fathers, and the cost of staying silent.
authorBio: Khaled Hosseini is an Afghan-American novelist and physician known for stories set against Afghanistan's recent history.

title: Life of Pi
author: Yann Martel
synopsis: After a shipwreck, a sixteen-year-old boy shares a lifeboat with a hyena, a zebra, an orangutan, and a Bengal tiger. What's left, once the animals sort themselves out, is a story about faith, survival, and which version of events you choose to believe.
authorBio: Yann Martel is a Canadian author whose fiction often circles questions of belief and storytelling itself.

title: The God of Small Things
author: Arundhati Roy
synopsis: Twins Estha and Rahel grow up in Kerala under the weight of family secrets and the rigid lines of caste, love, and law that the novel calls the 'Love Laws.' Told in looping, non-linear prose that circles a single tragic summer.
authorBio: Arundhati Roy is an Indian author and essayist; this Booker Prize-winning debut remains her best-known novel.
staffNote: Reread it every monsoon. Still finds something new. — A.

title: A Suitable Boy
author: Vikram Seth
synopsis: Four families, one determined mother, and newly independent India form the backdrop to Lata's search for a husband she can actually love. Sprawling in the best sense — settle in for the long haul.
authorBio: Vikram Seth is an Indian novelist and poet celebrated for his range, from verse novels to this doorstop of a social epic.

title: Midnight's Children
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: Born at the exact moment of India's independence, Saleem Sinai finds his life mysteriously tangled up with his newborn nation's fate. Magical realism, historical satire, and a thousand telescoping asides.
authorBio: Salman Rushdie is a British-Indian novelist whose fiction fuses history, myth, and politics.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
synopsis: How did an unremarkable ape end up running the planet? Harari walks through the cognitive, agricultural, and scientific revolutions that got us here, and asks what we've actually gained.
authorBio: Yuval Noah Harari is an Israeli historian whose big-picture books have become a global phenomenon.
staffNote: Every conversation for a month after finishing this. Fair warning. — R.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
synopsis: Raised by survivalist parents in rural Idaho with no birth certificate and no schooling, Westover eventually taught herself enough to leave for university. A memoir about the price of leaving where you're from.
authorBio: Tara Westover is an American author and historian; this is her first book.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
author: Rebecca Skloot
synopsis: In 1951 doctors took cells from a poor Black tobacco farmer without her knowledge; those cells are still alive today, multiplied into tons of tissue used in labs worldwide. Skloot traces the science and the family left out of it.
authorBio: Rebecca Skloot is an American science journalist; this was a decade-long project.

title: Into Thin Air
author: Jon Krakauer
synopsis: Krakauer was on Everest as a journalist in 1996 when a sudden storm killed eight climbers in a single day. His account of what went wrong is as much about ambition as it is about weather.
authorBio: Jon Krakauer is an American writer and mountaineer known for reporting from inside the stories he covers.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
synopsis: A Nobel laureate explains the two systems running your brain — one fast and intuitive, one slow and deliberate — and all the ways the fast one gets you into trouble.
authorBio: Daniel Kahneman was a psychologist and Nobel laureate in Economics, a founder of behavioral economics.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
synopsis: Black holes, the Big Bang, and the shape of time itself, explained without requiring a physics degree. Still the book most people mean when they say they want to 'understand the universe better.'
authorBio: Stephen Hawking was a theoretical physicist and cosmologist, and one of the best-selling science writers of all time.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
synopsis: A disgraced journalist and a hacker with a photographic memory dig into a forty-year-old disappearance, and find a family with far worse secrets than a missing heiress.
authorBio: Stieg Larsson was a Swedish journalist; this was the first of his Millennium trilogy, published after his death.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
synopsis: On their fifth wedding anniversary, Amy disappears, and every clue points at her husband Nick. Told in alternating, increasingly unreliable voices — trust no one, including the narrators.
authorBio: Gillian Flynn is an American writer known for sharp, morally slippery thrillers.
staffNote: Do not read the last page early. Just don't. — S.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
synopsis: Ten strangers are lured to an island and picked off one by one, each death matching a line from an old nursery rhyme. The best-selling mystery novel ever written, and still the blueprint for the genre.
authorBio: Agatha Christie was an English writer, the best-selling novelist of all time.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
synopsis: A woman shoots her husband five times and never speaks again. Her new therapist becomes obsessed with making her talk, and with the night that broke her silence in the first place.
authorBio: Alex Michaelides is a British-Cypriot author and screenwriter; this was his debut novel.

title: Sherlock Holmes: The Complete Novels
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
synopsis: All four Holmes novels in one volume, from a locked-room disappearance to a hound stalking the Devon moors. The consulting detective who taught every mystery writer since how deduction should sound.
authorBio: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle was a British writer and physician best known for creating Sherlock Holmes.

title: Big Little Lies
author: Liane Moriarty
synopsis: Three mothers at the school gate, one trivia-night death, and a small coastal town full of secrets that were never as hidden as everyone thought. Funny and sharp until it suddenly isn't.
authorBio: Liane Moriarty is an Australian author known for domestic dramas with a thriller's pacing.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
synopsis: On the desert planet Arrakis, a boy raised for greatness inherits a war over the most valuable substance in the universe. Empire, ecology, and prophecy, tangled together in the sand.
authorBio: Frank Herbert was an American science fiction writer; Dune remains one of the best-selling sci-fi novels ever published.
staffNote: Give it 100 pages. Then you won't be able to stop. — R.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
synopsis: Stranded alone on Mars with a limited supply of food and a botanist's stubbornness, Mark Watney has to science his way through survival, one problem at a time. Funnier than a story about dying alone on Mars has any right to be.
authorBio: Andy Weir is an American author who self-published this before it became a bestseller.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
synopsis: A washed-up hacker is hired for one last job jacking into a system built to keep him out. The novel that coined 'cyberspace' and shaped every hacker story that followed.
authorBio: William Gibson is an American-Canadian writer credited as a founder of the cyberpunk genre.

title: Ender's Game
author: Orson Scott Card
synopsis: A gifted child is recruited into a military academy in orbit, trained through war games for a conflict he doesn't fully understand. What looks like strategy fiction turns into something much sadder.
authorBio: Orson Scott Card is an American author; this novel won both the Hugo and Nebula awards.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
synopsis: A man wakes up alone on a spacecraft with no memory of how he got there or why the fate of Earth depends on him finishing the mission. A puzzle box of a novel, one discovery at a time.
authorBio: Andy Weir is an American author known for meticulously researched, problem-solving science fiction.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
synopsis: A future where everyone is engineered for their role and kept content with a drug called soma — no rebellion required, because nobody wants to rebel. The dystopia that predicted comfort, not cruelty, as the real threat.
authorBio: Aldous Huxley was an English writer whose 1932 novel remains a cornerstone of dystopian fiction.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
synopsis: Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy spend five hundred pages misjudging each other before working out that they were wrong. Still the reigning template for every enemies-to-lovers plot written since.
authorBio: Jane Austen was an English novelist whose social comedies of manners remain endlessly rereadable.

title: The Notebook
author: Nicholas Sparks
synopsis: An old man reads a love story aloud to a woman in a nursing home, not telling her at first that the story is theirs. A summer romance that survives war, class, and decades apart.
authorBio: Nicholas Sparks is an American author known for sentimental, small-town romances.

title: Normal People
author: Sally Rooney
synopsis: Connell and Marianne keep finding and losing each other from secondary school through university, never quite able to say what they mean out loud. Quiet, precise, and a little devastating.
authorBio: Sally Rooney is an Irish author known for spare, emotionally exact prose about young adulthood.
staffNote: Will ruin you for two days. Worth it. — A.

title: Me Before You
author: Jojo Moyes
synopsis: A cheerful, directionless young woman takes a job caring for a man who was once an adventurer and is now determined to end his life. Neither of them expects to change the other's mind about anything.
authorBio: Jojo Moyes is a British author and journalist writing across romance and contemporary fiction.

title: Beach Read
author: Emily Henry
synopsis: A literary novelist with writer's block and a commercial romance writer end up in neighboring lake houses and strike a dare: swap genres for the summer. Neither of them saw the ending coming, themselves included.
authorBio: Emily Henry is an American author known for witty, feelings-forward contemporary romance.

title: It Ends With Us
author: Colleen Hoover
synopsis: Lily builds the life and business she always wanted, then falls for a neurosurgeon whose charm hides something she recognizes from her childhood. A romance that turns into something much harder to read.
authorBio: Colleen Hoover is an American author whose emotionally intense novels have topped bestseller lists worldwide.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
synopsis: Small, boring, one-percent changes compound into identity-level transformation, if you build the systems right. Clear turns habit formation into something closer to engineering than willpower.
authorBio: James Clear is an American author and speaker focused on habits, decision-making, and continuous improvement.
staffNote: The one book everyone actually finishes and uses. — S.

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
synopsis: Most suffering, Tolle argues, comes from living in your head instead of in the present moment. A slow, meditative argument for stepping out of the noise of your own thoughts.
authorBio: Eckhart Tolle is a German-born spiritual teacher and author.

title: Ikigai: The Japanese Secret to a Long and Happy Life
author: Héctor García
synopsis: On a small Japanese island with an unusually high number of centenarians, the authors go looking for the secret and find it has less to do with diet than with purpose. Short, gentle, and hard to argue with.
authorBio: Héctor García is a Spanish author living in Japan, writing on Japanese culture and philosophy.

title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
author: Mark Manson
synopsis: A counterargument to relentless positivity: you only have so many cares to give, so give them on purpose. Blunt, funny, and more useful than the title lets on.
authorBio: Mark Manson is an American blogger and author writing on self-improvement without the usual polish.

title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
synopsis: Focused, undistracted work is becoming rare and, Newport argues, more valuable because of it. A practical case for closing the tabs and actually finishing something.
authorBio: Cal Newport is an American computer science professor and author writing on focus and productivity.

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
author: Stephen R. Covey
synopsis: Covey's principle-centered approach to personal effectiveness, still handed out in offices decades later. Less about tricks, more about character — his word, repeated often.
authorBio: Stephen R. Covey was an American author and educator focused on leadership and personal development.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
synopsis: Scout Finch watches her father defend a Black man falsely accused in 1930s Alabama, and grows up faster than a childhood summer should allow. Told with a child's clarity about a very adult failure of justice.
authorBio: Harper Lee was an American novelist; this was her first published novel and remains a staple of school reading lists.

author: George Orwell
synopsis: Winston Smith rewrites history for a living, in a state that watches everything and permits nothing, including thought. The novel that gave us Big Brother, doublethink, and a vocabulary for surveillance we still reach for.
authorBio: George Orwell was an English novelist and essayist, one of the most influential political writers of the 20th century.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
synopsis: Jay Gatsby throws enormous parties for a guest who almost never comes, chasing a version of the past that was never really his to reclaim. Slim, glittering, and quietly bitter about the American dream.
authorBio: F. Scott Fitzgerald was an American novelist whose Jazz Age fiction defined a generation.
staffNote: Read it in one sitting or not at all. — R.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
synopsis: An orphaned governess with a sharp mind and a firmer spine falls for her brooding employer, then discovers exactly why she shouldn't. Gothic, proto-feminist, and still swoon-worthy two centuries later.
authorBio: Charlotte Brontë was an English novelist; Jane Eyre is considered one of the great works of English literature.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
synopsis: A destitute former student convinces himself that murdering a pawnbroker is justified by a higher morality, then spends the rest of the novel unable to live with what he's done. Guilt has rarely been rendered this vividly.
authorBio: Fyodor Dostoevsky was a Russian novelist whose psychological fiction remains foundational to the form.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
synopsis: Seven generations of the Buendía family live and repeat their way through the rise and fall of the town of Macondo. The novel that made magical realism a household term, one impossible detail at a time.
authorBio: Gabriel García Márquez was a Colombian novelist and Nobel laureate.

title: Charlotte's Web
author: E. B. White
synopsis: A pig named Wilbur is saved from the chopping block by a spider who writes his praises into her web. A gentle, honest introduction to friendship, and to loss.
authorBio: E. B. White was an American writer and longtime contributor to The New Yorker.
staffNote: Bring a tissue for the grown-up reading it aloud, not just the kid. — A.

title: Matilda
author: Roald Dahl
synopsis: A brilliant five-year-old with neglectful parents and a tyrannical headmistress discovers she has a little telekinetic help of her own. Dahl at his sharpest about how unfair childhood can be, and how satisfying it is to fix that.
authorBio: Roald Dahl was a British author of children's fiction known for gleeful, subversive storytelling.

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
author: Eric Carle
synopsis: A tiny caterpillar eats his way through a very specific and very large list of foods before turning into a butterfly. Bright collage art and a counting lesson tucked into a story that's been read aloud for generations.
authorBio: Eric Carle was an American illustrator and writer known for his distinctive tissue-paper collage style.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
author: J. K. Rowling
synopsis: An eleven-year-old discovers on his birthday that he's a wizard, that his parents were murdered by a dark one, and that he has a scar with a rather significant backstory. Where it all began.
authorBio: J. K. Rowling is a British author whose seven-book series became a global publishing phenomenon.

title: Where the Wild Things Are
author: Maurice Sendak
synopsis: Sent to bed without supper, Max sails to an island of monsters and is crowned their king, until he starts to miss home. A picture book about tantrums, imagination, and being loved anyway.
authorBio: Maurice Sendak was an American illustrator and writer, best known for this 1963 picture book.

title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
synopsis: A pilot stranded in the desert meets a small prince who has left his tiny asteroid to understand grown-ups, and finds them mostly baffling. A children's book that somehow makes more sense as an adult.
authorBio: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry was a French writer and aviator; this remains one of the best-selling books ever published.
staffNote: Not really for children. Don't tell them that. — S.

title: Coraline
author: Neil Gaiman
synopsis: A curious girl finds a door to another version of her home where everything looks better—until the other mother wants her to stay forever.
authorBio: Neil Gaiman is a British author known for fantasy, mythology, and dark children's fiction.

title: Percy Jackson and the Lightning Thief
author: Rick Riordan
synopsis: A twelve-year-old discovers he is a demigod and is sent on a quest to recover Zeus's stolen lightning bolt.
authorBio: Rick Riordan is an American author best known for myth-inspired middle-grade adventure series.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
synopsis: A reluctant hobbit joins a company of dwarves on a dangerous quest to reclaim a mountain kingdom from a dragon.
authorBio: J. R. R. Tolkien was an English writer and philologist who created Middle-earth.
staffNote: The gateway drug to fantasy. — R.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
synopsis: Four sisters grow up during the American Civil War, each trying to build a life that fits her ambitions, limitations, and family.
authorBio: Louisa May Alcott was an American novelist and essayist whose domestic fiction became a classic.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J. D. Salinger
synopsis: After being expelled from school, Holden Caulfield wanders New York while wrestling with grief, alienation, and his contempt for adulthood.
authorBio: J. D. Salinger was an American writer best known for this coming-of-age novel.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
synopsis: A beautiful young man remains outwardly young while a hidden portrait records the corruption caused by his pursuit of pleasure.
authorBio: Oscar Wilde was an Irish poet, playwright, and novelist celebrated for his wit and social satire.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
synopsis: Private reflections from a Roman emperor on discipline, mortality, duty, and keeping control of what actually belongs to you.
authorBio: Marcus Aurelius was Roman emperor and a major Stoic philosopher.

title: The Courage to Be Disliked
author: Ichiro Kishimi and Fumitake Koga
synopsis: A philosopher and a young man debate Adlerian psychology, responsibility, freedom, and the possibility of living without chasing approval.
authorBio: Ichiro Kishimi and Fumitake Koga are Japanese authors who popularized Adlerian ideas through dialogue.

title: Make Time
author: Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky
synopsis: A practical framework for choosing what deserves attention instead of letting every notification decide the shape of your day.
authorBio: Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky are designers and writers focused on productivity and attention.

title: The Power of Habit
author: Charles Duhigg
synopsis: Why habits form, how cue-routine-reward loops work, and what happens when people learn to redesign them.
authorBio: Charles Duhigg is an American journalist and author writing about habits and productivity.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
synopsis: A psychiatrist recounts surviving Nazi concentration camps and explains his view that meaning can help people endure profound suffering.
authorBio: Viktor E. Frankl was an Austrian psychiatrist and neurologist who founded logotherapy.

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
synopsis: A collection of stories and observations about how behavior, emotion, and luck shape financial decisions more than spreadsheets do.
authorBio: Morgan Housel is an American author and investor focused on behavioral finance.
staffNote: More useful than another finance formula sheet. — R.

title: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
synopsis: Between life and death, Nora Seed enters a library containing versions of her life based on different choices she could have made.
authorBio: Matt Haig is a British author whose fiction frequently explores regret, hope, and possibility.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
synopsis: A fireman whose job is to burn books begins to wonder why a society built on constant entertainment fears ideas so much.
authorBio: Ray Bradbury was an American author celebrated for imaginative science fiction and fantasy.

title: The Handmaid's Tale
author: Margaret Atwood
synopsis: In a theocratic future, women are stripped of rights and assigned roles designed to control reproduction, memory, and identity.
authorBio: Margaret Atwood is a Canadian author whose fiction often examines power, gender, and authoritarianism.

title: The Road
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: A father and son travel through a ruined America, carrying a fragile belief that goodness can survive the end of the world.
authorBio: Cormac McCarthy was an American novelist acclaimed for spare, uncompromising prose.

title: The Name of the Rose
author: Umberto Eco
synopsis: A Franciscan friar investigates a series of deaths in a medieval monastery where books may be more dangerous than weapons.
authorBio: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist, philosopher, and semiotician.

title: The Secret History
author: Donna Tartt
synopsis: A group of classics students at an elite college cross a moral line that cannot be uncrossed, then spend the aftermath trying to live with it.
authorBio: Donna Tartt is an American novelist known for psychologically detailed literary fiction.

title: The Book Thief
author: Markus Zusak
synopsis: In Nazi Germany, a young girl steals books while death watches her story unfold around the people she loves.
authorBio: Markus Zusak is an Australian novelist known for inventive historical fiction.
staffNote: Beautiful, brutal, and impossible to forget. — A.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
synopsis: A shepherd boy follows a recurring dream toward the Egyptian pyramids and discovers that the journey matters as much as the treasure.
authorBio: Paulo Coelho is a Brazilian novelist whose allegorical fiction has become internationally popular.

author: Rebecca Makkai

authorBio: Rebecca Makkai is an acclaimed author associated with memorable fiction and influential storytelling.

author: Edgar Allan Poe
synopsis: This single volume brings together all of Poe's stories and poems, and illuminates the diverse and multifaceted genius of one of the greatest and most influential figures in American literary history.
authorBio: Edgar Allan Poe is an author whose bibliography includes The Complete Stories and Poems, The Cask of Amontillado, and The Pit and the Pendulum, spanning Mystery.

This riveting, brilliant novel crackles with the fire of fierce defiance, forbidden romance, and the sparks of a revolution about to ignite.
authorBio: Lauren Oliver is an author whose bibliography includes Delirium, Before I Fall, and Pandemonium, spanning Romance and Sci-Fi.

title: The Silkworm
author: Robert Galbraith

authorBio: Robert Galbraith is an author whose bibliography includes The Cuckoo's Calling, The Silkworm, and Lethal White, spanning Mystery.

author: Nicholas Sparks
synopsis: Shimmering with suspense and emotional intensity - takes readers on a hunt for the truth about a man and his memories, and about both the heartbreaking fragility and enormous strength of love.Nicholas Sparks is our very best chronicler of the human heart. authorBio: Nicholas Sparks is an author whose bibliography includes Dear John, The Last Song, and The Lucky One, spanning Romance.

synopsis: It began with Eragon... It ends with Inheritance.Not so very long ago, Eragon - Shadeslayer, Dragon Rider - was nothing more than a poor farm boy, and his dragon, Saphira, only a blue stone in the forest.

author: Ally Condie
synopsis: The Society chooses everything. The books you read. The music you listen to. The person you love. Yet for Cassia the rules have changed. synopsis: The strange and wonderful tale of man's experiences on Mars, filled with intense images and astonishing visions. Now part of the Voyager Classics collection.The Martian Chronicles tells the story of humanity's repeated attempts to colonize the red planet.
authorBio: Ray Bradbury is an author whose bibliography includes The Martian Chronicles, The Illustrated Man, and Dandelion Wine, spanning Children's, Sci-Fi, and Self-Help.

synopsis: That's what Macy has to look forward to while her boyfriend, Jason, is away at Brain Camp. authorBio: Patrick Ness is an author whose bibliography includes A Monster Calls, The Knife of Never Letting Go, and The Ask and the Answer, spanning Children's, Romance, and Sci-Fi.

title: A Great and Terrible Beauty
author: Libba Bray

authorBio: Libba Bray is an author whose bibliography includes A Great and Terrible Beauty, Rebel Angels, and The Sweet Far Thing, spanning Fantasy, Fiction, and Romance.

title: Drums of Autumn
author: Diana Gabaldon
synopsis: In this breathtaking novel, rich in history and adventure, #1 New York Times bestselling author Diana Gabaldon continues the story of Claire Randall and Jamie Fraser that started with the now-classic novel Outlander and continued in Dragonfly in Amber and Voyager. authorBio: Diana Gabaldon is an author whose bibliography includes Dragonfly in Amber, Voyager, and Drums of Autumn, spanning Romance.
staffNote: A strong bookstore pick for readers of romance.

title: Words of Radiance
author: Brandon Sanderson

Now he must protect the king and Dalinar from every common peril as well as the distinctly uncommon threat of the Assassin, all while secretly struggling to master remarkable new powers that are somehow linked...
authorBio: Brandon Sanderson is an author whose bibliography includes The Final Empire, The Way of Kings, and The Well of Ascension, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Carry On
author: Rainbow Rowell
synopsis: Simon Snow is the worst Chosen One who's ever been chosen.That's what his roommate, Baz, says. And Baz might be evil and a vampire and a complete git, but he's probably right.Half the time, Simon can't even make his wand work, and the other half, he starts something on fire.
authorBio: Rainbow Rowell is an author whose bibliography includes Carry On, Attachments, and Landline, spanning Romance.

author: John Irving

It is a novel rich with "lunacy and sorrow"; yet the dark, violent events of the story do not undermine a comedy both ribald and robust. In more than thirty languages, in more than forty countries-with more than ten million copies in print-this novel provides almost
authorBio: John Irving is an author whose bibliography includes A Prayer for Owen Meany, The World According to Garp, and The Cider House Rules, spanning Classics.

title: Something Blue
author: Emily Giffin
synopsis: Following the smash-hit Something Borrowed comes story of betrayal, redemption, and forgiveness Darcy Rhone has always been able to rely on a few things: Her beauty and charm. Her fiance, Dex.
authorBio: Emily Giffin is an author whose bibliography includes Something Borrowed, Something Blue, and Love the One You're With, spanning Romance.

authorBio: Marie Lu is an author whose bibliography includes Prodigy, Champion, and The Young Elites, spanning Sci-Fi.

authorBio: Jennifer Weiner is an author whose bibliography includes Good in Bed, In Her Shoes, and Little Earthquakes, spanning Romance.

author: Kate Atkinson
synopsis: What if you could live again and again, until you got it right? On a cold and snowy night in 1910, Ursula Todd is born to an English banker and his wife.

title: I've Got Your Number

She is about to marry her ideal man, Magnus Tavish, but in one afternoon her "happily ever after" begins to fall apart. Not only has she lost her engagement ring in a hotel fire drill but in the panic that f
authorBio: Sophie Kinsella is an author whose bibliography includes Confessions of a Shopaholic, Can You Keep a Secret?, and The Undomestic Goddess, spanning Romance.

author: Marissa Meyer

authorBio: Marissa Meyer is an author whose bibliography includes Scarlet, Cress, and Winter, spanning Romance and Sci-Fi.

title: The Pearl

authorBio: Sarah Dessen is an author whose bibliography includes Just Listen, The Truth About Forever, and Along for the Ride, spanning Romance.

authorBio: Jojo Moyes is an author whose bibliography includes After You, The Giver of Stars, and One Plus One, spanning Romance.

How much I'd been threatened, or just how dark and desperate the shadow of our pasts would become.Entwined by our secrets, we tried to defy the odds. title: From Dead to Worse

title: High Fidelity

He can just do what he wants when he wants: like listen to whatever music he likes, look up the girls that are on his list, and generally behaves as if Laura never mattered. authorBio: Nick Hornby is an author whose bibliography includes High Fidelity, A Long Way Down, and How to Be Good, spanning Classics and Romance.

title: I'd Tell You I Love You, But Then I'd Have to Kill You

title: The Bluest Eye

title: The Storyteller

When Josef Weber, an elderly man in Sage's grief support group, begins stopping by the bakery, they strike up an unlikely friendship. Despite their differences, they see in each other the hidden scars that others can't, and they become companions.Everything changes on the day that Josef confesses a l

title: The Rainmaker

author: Robert A. Heinlein
synopsis: It is a tale of revolution, of the rebellion of a former penal colony on the Moon against its masters on the Earth. It is a tale of a culture whose family structures are based on the presence of two men for every woman, leading to novel forms of marriage and family.
authorBio: Robert A. Heinlein is an author whose bibliography includes Stranger in a Strange Land, The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress, and The Puppet Masters, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: School's Out—Forever
author: James Patterson
synopsis: In this eagerly awaited follow-up, brave bird-kid Max and her flock are discovered by an FBI agent and forced to go to "school." There is no such thing as an ordinary day as Max deciphers how and when she's supposed to save the world, and she faces her greatest enemy--a clone of herself. Little, Brown and Company
authorBio: James Patterson is an author whose bibliography includes Along Came a Spider, Kiss the Girls, and 1st to Die, spanning Mystery and Sci-Fi.

title: Cannery Row
author: John Steinbeck
synopsis: Cannery Row is a book without much of a plot. Rather, it is an attempt to capture the feeling and people of a place, the cannery district of Monterey, California, which is populated by a mix of those down on their luck and those who choose for other reasons not to live "up the hill" in the more respectable area of town.
authorBio: John Steinbeck is an author whose bibliography includes The Pearl, Cannery Row, and Travels with Charley: In Search of America, spanning Classics.

title: Among the Hidden
author: Margaret Peterson Haddix
synopsis: SHADOW CHILDRENLuke has never been to school. He's never had a birthday party, or gone to a friend's house for an overnight.
authorBio: Margaret Peterson Haddix is an author whose bibliography includes Among the Hidden, Into the Gauntlet, and Found, spanning Children's.

title: The Essential Calvin and Hobbes: A Calvin and Hobbes Treasury
author: Bill Watterson
synopsis: Perhaps the most brilliant comic strip ever created, Calvin and Hobbes continues to entertain with dazzling cartooning and tremendous humor.Bill Watterson's Calvin and Hobbes has been a worldwide favorite since its introduction in 1985. The strip follows the richly imaginative adventures of Calvin and his trusty tiger, Hobbes.
authorBio: Bill Watterson is an author whose bibliography includes The Essential Calvin and Hobbes: A Calvin and Hobbes Treasury, The Calvin and Hobbes Tenth Anniversary Book, and The Complete Calvin and Hobbes, spanning Children's.

title: The Marriage Plot
author: Jeffrey Eugenides
synopsis: It's the early 1980s - the country is in a deep recession, and life after college is harder than ever. In the cafés on College Hill, the wised-up kids are inhaling Derrida and listening to the Talking Heads.
authorBio: Jeffrey Eugenides is an author whose bibliography includes Middlesex, The Virgin Suicides, and The Marriage Plot, spanning Classics and Romance.

title: Rise of the Evening Star
author: Brandon Mull
synopsis: At the end of the school year, Kendra and her brother Seth find themselves racing back to Fablehaven, a refuge for mythical and magical creatures. Grandpa Sorenson, the caretaker, invites three specialists -- a potion master, a magical relics collector, and a mystical creature trapper -- to help protect the property from the Society of the Evening Star, an ancient organization determined to infiltrate the preserve and steal a hidden artifact of great power.
authorBio: Brandon Mull is an author whose bibliography includes Fablehaven, Rise of the Evening Star, and Grip of the Shadow Plague, spanning Children's.

title: Blood Rites
author: Jim Butcher
synopsis: For Harry Dresden, Chicago's only professional wizard, there have been worse assignments than going undercover on the set of an adult film. Dodging flaming monkey poo, for instance.
authorBio: Jim Butcher is an author whose bibliography includes Grave Peril, Blood Rites, and Proven Guilty, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Alias Grace
author: Margaret Atwood
synopsis: It's 1843, and Grace Marks has been convicted for her involvement in the vicious murders of her employer and his housekeeper and mistress. Some believe Grace is innocent; others think her evil or insane.
authorBio: Margaret Atwood is an author whose bibliography includes Oryx and Crake, Alias Grace, and The Year of the Flood, spanning Classics, Mystery, and Sci-Fi.

title: It's Not Summer Without You
author: Jenny Han
synopsis: Belly finds out what comes after falling in love in this follow-up to The Summer I Turned Pretty from the New York Times bestselling author of To All the Boys I've Loved Before (soon to be a major motion picture!), Jenny Han.Can summer be truly summer without Cousins Beach?It used to be that Belly counted the days until summer, until she was back at Cousins Beach with Conrad and Jeremiah. But not this year.
authorBio: Jenny Han is an author whose bibliography includes P.S. I Still Love You, The Summer I Turned Pretty, and Always and Forever, Lara Jean, spanning Romance.

title: Sputnik Sweetheart
author: Haruki Murakami, Philip Gabriel (Translator)
synopsis: alternate cover can be found hereSumire is in love with a woman seventeen years her senior. But whereas Miu is glamorous and successful, Sumire is an aspiring writer who dresses in an oversized second-hand coat and heavy boots like a character in a Kerouac novel.Sumire spends hours on the phone talking to her best friend K about the big questions in life: what is sexual desire, and should she ever tell Miu how she feels for her?
authorBio: Haruki Murakami, Philip Gabriel (Translator) is an author whose bibliography includes Kafka on the Shore, Sputnik Sweetheart, and What I Talk About When I Talk About Running, spanning Classics and Romance.

title: Mostly Harmless
author: Douglas Adams
synopsis: It's easy to get disheartened when your planet has been blown up, the woman you love has vanished due to a misunderstanding about space/time, the spaceship you are on crashes on a remote and Bob-fearing planet, and all you have to fall back on are a few simple sandwich-making skills. However, instead of being disheartened, Arthur Dent makes the terrible mistake of starting to enjoy life a bit-and immediately all hell breaks loose.Hell takes a number of forms: there's the standard Ford Prefect version, in the...
authorBio: Douglas Adams is an author whose bibliography includes The Ultimate Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Life, the Universe and Everything, and Mostly Harmless, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Dead Wake: The Last Crossing of the Lusitania
author: Erik Larson
synopsis: From the #1 New York Times bestselling author and master of narrative nonfiction comes the enthralling story of the sinking of the LusitaniaOn May 1, 1915, a luxury ocean liner as richly appointed as an English country house sailed out of New York, bound for Liverpool, carrying a record number of children and infants. The passengers were anxious.
authorBio: Erik Larson is an author whose bibliography includes The Devil in the White City: Murder, Magic, and Madness at the Fair That Changed America, In the Garden of Beasts: Love, Terror, and an American Family in Hitler's Berlin, and Dead Wake: The Last Crossing of the Lusitania, spanning Classics, Mystery, and Non-Fiction.

title: Inkspell
author: Cornelia Funke, Anthea Bell (Translator)
synopsis: The captivating sequel to INKHEART, the critically acclaimed, international bestseller by Cornelia Funke, an author who is emerging as a truly modern classic writer for children.Although a year has passed, not a day goes by without Meggie thinking of INKHEART, the book whose characters became real. But for Dustfinger, the fire-eater brought into being from words, the need to return to the tale has become desperate.
authorBio: Cornelia Funke, Anthea Bell (Translator) is an author whose bibliography includes Inkheart, Inkspell, and Inkdeath, spanning Children's.

title: Holidays on Ice
author: David Sedaris
synopsis: David Sedaris's beloved holiday collection is new again with six more pieces, including a never before published story. Along with such favorites as the diaries of a Macy's elf and the annals of two very competitive families, are Sedaris's tales of tardy trick-or-treaters (Us and Them); the difficulties of explaining the Easter Bunny to the French (Jesus Shaves); what to do when you've been locked out in a snowstorm (Let It Snow); the puzzling Christmas traditions of other nations (Six to Eight Black Men); what...
authorBio: David Sedaris is an author whose bibliography includes Me Talk Pretty One Day, Dress Your Family in Corduroy and Denim, and When You Are Engulfed in Flames, spanning Non-Fiction.

title: Recursion
author: Blake Crouch
synopsis: Memory makes reality.That's what New York City cop Barry Sutton is learning as he investigates the devastating phenomenon the media has dubbed False Memory Syndrome-a mysterious affliction that drives its victims mad with memories of a life they never lived.That's what neuroscientist Helena Smith believes. It's why she's dedicated her life to creating a technology that will let us preserve our most precious memories.
authorBio: Blake Crouch is an author whose bibliography includes Dark Matter, Recursion, and Wayward, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Memory Man
author: David Baldacci
synopsis: Amos Decker's life changed forever--twice.The first time was on the gridiron. A big, towering athlete, he was the only person from his hometown of Burlington ever to go pro.
authorBio: David Baldacci is an author whose bibliography includes Memory Man, Absolute Power, and The Innocent, spanning Mystery.

title: The Young Elites
author: Marie Lu
synopsis: I am tired of being used, hurt, and cast aside.Adelina Amouteru is a survivor of the blood fever. A decade ago, the deadly illness swept through her nation.
authorBio: Marie Lu is an author whose bibliography includes Prodigy, Champion, and The Young Elites, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Survivor
author: Chuck Palahniuk
synopsis: From the author of the underground sensation Fight Club comes this wickedly incisive second novel, a mesmerizing, unnerving, and hilarious vision of cult and post-cult life.Tender Branson-last surviving member of the so-called Creedish Death Cult-is dictating his life story into the flight recorder of Flight 2039, cruising on autopilot at 39,000 feet somewhere over the Pacific Ocean. He is all alone in the airplane, which will crash shortly into the vast Australian outback.
authorBio: Chuck Palahniuk is an author whose bibliography includes Fight Club, Choke, and Invisible Monsters, spanning Classics and Mystery.

title: Wintergirls
author: Laurie Halse Anderson
synopsis: "Dead girl walking," the boys say in the halls."Tell us your secret," the girls whisper, one toilet to another.I am that girl.I am the space between my thighs, daylight shining through.I am the bones they want, wired on a porcelain frame. Lia and Cassie are best friends, wintergirls frozen in matchstick bodies, competitors in a deadly contest to see who can be the skinniest.
authorBio: Laurie Halse Anderson is an author whose bibliography includes Speak, Wintergirls, and Fever 1793, spanning Children's, Fiction, and Romance.

title: Lirael
author: Garth Nix
synopsis: Lirael has never felt like a true daughter of the Clayr. Now, two years past the time when she should have received the Sight that is the Clayr's birthright, she feels alone, abandoned, unsure of who she is.
authorBio: Garth Nix is an author whose bibliography includes Abhorsen, Lirael, and Mister Monday, spanning Children's and Sci-Fi.

title: The Hypnotist's Love Story
author: Liane Moriarty
synopsis: Ellen O'Farrell is a professional hypnotherapist who works out of the eccentric beachfront home she inherited from her grandparents. It's a nice life, except for her tumultuous relationship history.
authorBio: Liane Moriarty is an author whose bibliography includes The Husband's Secret, What Alice Forgot, and Nine Perfect Strangers, spanning Mystery.

title: To the Nines
author: Janet Evanovich
synopsis: Stephanie Plum's got rent to pay, people shooting at her, and psychos wanting her dead every day of the week (much to the dismay of her mother, her family, the men in her life, the guy who slices meat at the deli...oh, the list goes on). An ordinary person would cave under the pressure.But hey, she's from Jersey.Stephanie Plum may not be the best bounty hunter in beautiful downtown Trenton, but she's pretty darn good at turning bad situations her way...and she always gets her man.
authorBio: Janet Evanovich is an author whose bibliography includes One for the Money, Two for the Dough, and Hot Six, spanning Mystery.
staffNote: A strong bookstore pick for readers of mystery.

title: The Death of Mrs. Westaway
author: Ruth Ware
synopsis: On a day that begins like any other, Hal receives a mysterious letter bequeathing her a substantial inheritance. She realizes very quickly that the letter was sent to the wrong person-but also that the cold-reading skills she's honed as a tarot card reader might help her claim the money.Soon, Hal finds herself at the funeral of the deceased…where it dawns on her that there is something very, very wrong about this strange situation and the inheritance at the centre of it.
authorBio: Ruth Ware is an author whose bibliography includes The Woman in Cabin 10, In a Dark, Dark Wood, and The Turn of the Key, spanning Mystery.

title: What I Talk About When I Talk About Running
author: Haruki Murakami, Philip Gabriel (Translator)
synopsis: In 1982, having sold his jazz bar to devote himself to writing, Murakami began running to keep fit. A year later, he'd completed a solo course from Athens to Marathon, and now, after dozens of such races, not to mention triathlons and a dozen critically acclaimed books, he reflects upon the influence the sport has had on his life and--even more important--on his writing.
authorBio: Haruki Murakami, Philip Gabriel (Translator) is an author whose bibliography includes Kafka on the Shore, Sputnik Sweetheart, and What I Talk About When I Talk About Running, spanning Classics and Romance.

title: Rebel Angels
author: Libba Bray
synopsis: Ah, Christmas! Gemma Doyle is looking forward to a holiday from Spence Academy, spending time with her friends in the city, attending ritzy balls, and on a somber note, tending to her ailing father.
authorBio: Libba Bray is an author whose bibliography includes A Great and Terrible Beauty, Rebel Angels, and The Sweet Far Thing, spanning Fantasy, Fiction, and Romance.

title: Stone of Tears
author: Terry Goodkind
synopsis: In Wizard's First Rule, Richard Cypher's world was turned upside down. Once a simple woods guide, Richard was forced to become the Seeker of Truth, to save the world from the vile dominance of Darken Rahl, the most viciously savage and powerful wizard the world had ever seen.
authorBio: Terry Goodkind is an author whose bibliography includes Wizard's First Rule, Stone of Tears, and Confessor, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: A Dirty Job
author: Christopher Moore
synopsis: Charlie Asher is a pretty normal guy with a normal life, married to a bright and pretty woman who actually loves him for his normalcy. They're even about to have their first child.
authorBio: Christopher Moore is an author whose bibliography includes Lamb: The Gospel According to Biff, Christ's Childhood Pal, A Dirty Job, and Bloodsucking Fiends, spanning Fantasy and Romance.

title: Fever 1793
author: Laurie Halse Anderson
synopsis: It's late summer 1793, and the streets of Philadelphia are abuzz with mosquitoes and rumors of fever. Down near the docks, many have taken ill, and the fatalities are mounting.
authorBio: Laurie Halse Anderson is an author whose bibliography includes Speak, Wintergirls, and Fever 1793, spanning Children's, Fiction, and Romance.

title: Fantastic Mr. Fox
author: Roald Dahl, Quentin Blake (Illustrator)
synopsis: Fantastic Mr. Fox is on the run! The three meanest farmers around are out to get him. Fat Boggis, squat Bunce, and skinny Bean have joined forces, and they have Mr. Fox and his family surrounded. What they don't know is that they're not dealing with just any fox-Mr. Fox would never surrender. But only the most fantastic plan ever can save him now.
authorBio: Roald Dahl, Quentin Blake (Illustrator) is an author whose bibliography includes James and the Giant Peach, The BFG, and The Witches, spanning Children's.

title: The Year of the Flood
author: Margaret Atwood
synopsis: The times and species have been changing at a rapid rate, and the social compact is wearing as thin as environmental stability. Adam One, the kindly leader of the God's Gardeners--a religion devoted to the melding of science and religion, as well as the preservation of all plant and animal life--has long predicted a natural disaster that will alter Earth as we know it.
authorBio: Margaret Atwood is an author whose bibliography includes Oryx and Crake, Alias Grace, and The Year of the Flood, spanning Classics, Mystery, and Sci-Fi.

title: Princess Academy
author: Shannon Hale
synopsis: Miri lives on a mountain where, for generations, her ancestors have quarried stone and lived a simple life. Then word comes that the king's priests have divined her small village the home of the future princess.
authorBio: Shannon Hale is an author whose bibliography includes The Goose Girl, Princess Academy, and Austenland, spanning Children's and Romance.

title: Lover Avenged
author: J.R. Ward
synopsis: Rehvenge has always kept his distance from the Brotherhood-even though his sister is married to a member, for he harbors a deadly secret that could make him a huge liability in their war against the lessers. As plots within and outside of the Brotherhood threaten to reveal the truth about Rehvenge, he turns to the only source of light in his darkening world, Ehlena, a vampire untouched by the corruption that has its hold on him-and the only thing standing between him and eternal destruction.
authorBio: J.R. Ward is an author whose bibliography includes Lover Avenged, Lover Mine, and Lover Unleashed, spanning Romance.

title: Proven Guilty
author: Jim Butcher
synopsis: There's no love lost between Harry Dresden, the only wizard in the Chicago phone book, and the White Council of Wizards, who find him brash and undisciplined. But war with the vampires has thinned their ranks, so the Council has drafted Harry as a Warden and assigned him to look into rumors of black magic in the Windy City.As Harry adjusts to his new role, another problem arrives in the form of the tattooed and pierced daughter of an old friend, all grown-up and already in trouble.
authorBio: Jim Butcher is an author whose bibliography includes Grave Peril, Blood Rites, and Proven Guilty, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Love, Rosie
author: Cecelia Ahern
synopsis: Sometimes you have to look at life in a whole new way...From the bestselling author of PS, I Love You comes a delightfully enchanting novel about what happens when two people who are meant to be together just can't seem to get it right.Rosie and Alex are destined for one another, and everyone seems to know it but them. Best friends since childhood, their relationship gets closer by the day, until Alex gets the news that his family is leaving Dublin and moving to Boston.
authorBio: Cecelia Ahern is an author whose bibliography includes P.S. I Love You, Love, Rosie, and Thanks for the Memories, spanning Mystery and Romance.

title: Heart of the Matter
author: Emily Giffin
synopsis: Tessa Russo is the mother of two young children and the wife of a renowned pediatric surgeon. Despite her own mother's warnings, Tessa has recently given up her career to focus on her family and the pursuit of domestic happiness.
authorBio: Emily Giffin is an author whose bibliography includes Something Borrowed, Something Blue, and Love the One You're With, spanning Romance.

title: Extras
author: Scott Westerfeld
synopsis: A few years after rebel Tally Youngblood takes down the Specials regime, a cultural renaissance sweeps the world. "Tech-heads" flaunt their latest gadgets, "kickers" spread gossip and trends, and "surge monkeys" are hooked on extreme plastic surgery.
authorBio: Scott Westerfeld is an author whose bibliography includes Uglies, Pretties, and Specials, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: White Night
author: Jim Butcher
synopsis: The inspiration for the Sci Fi channel television series In Chicago, someone has been killing practitioners of magic, those incapable of becoming full-fledged wizards. Shockingly, all the evidence points to Harry Dresden's half-brother, Thomas, as the murderer.
authorBio: Jim Butcher is an author whose bibliography includes Grave Peril, Blood Rites, and Proven Guilty, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: The Burning Bridge
author: John Flanagan
synopsis: Bracing for a final clash with the evil warlord Morgarath, the Rangers rally the kingdom's allies, and Will is chosen, along with his friend Horace, as special envoys to nearby Celtica. But the simple mission soon takes an unsettling turn - the Celticans have disappeared, their town abandoned.
authorBio: John Flanagan is an author whose bibliography includes The Ruins of Gorlan, The Burning Bridge, and The Battle for Skandia, spanning Children's.
staffNote: A strong bookstore pick for readers of children's.

title: Lover Mine
author: J.R. Ward
synopsis: John Matthew has come a long way since he was found living among humans, his vampire nature unknown to himself and to those around him. After he was taken in by the Brotherhood, no one could guess what his true history was- or his true identity.
authorBio: J.R. Ward is an author whose bibliography includes Lover Avenged, Lover Mine, and Lover Unleashed, spanning Romance.

title: The Ugly Truth
author: Jeff Kinney
synopsis: Greg Heffley has always been in a hurry to grow up. But is getting older really all it's cracked up to be?Greg suddenly finds himself dealing with the pressures of boy-girl parties, increased responsibilities, and even the awkward changes that come with getting older-all without his best friend, Rowley, at his side.
authorBio: Jeff Kinney is an author whose bibliography includes Diary of a Wimpy Kid, Rodrick Rules, and The Last Straw, spanning Children's.

title: The House at Riverton
author: Kate Morton
synopsis: The House at Riverton is a gorgeous debut novel set in England between the wars. Perfect for fans of "Downton Abbey," it's the story of an aristocratic family, a house, a mysterious death, and a way of life that vanished forever, told in flashback by a woman who witnessed it all.The novel is full of secrets - some revealed, others hidden forever, reminiscent of the romantic suspense of Daphne du Maurier.
authorBio: Kate Morton is an author whose bibliography includes The Forgotten Garden, The Secret Keeper, and The House at Riverton, spanning Mystery.

title: The Enemy
author: Lee Child
synopsis: Jack Reacher. Hero. Loner. Soldier. Soldier's son. An elite military cop, he was one of the army's brightest stars. But in every cop's life there is a turning point. One case. One messy, tangled case that can shatter a career. Turn a lawman into a renegade. And make him question words like honor, valor, and duty. For Jack Reacher, this is that case.New Year's Day, 1990. The Berlin Wall is coming down. The world is changing. And in a North Carolina "hot-sheets" motel, a two-star general is found dead. His briefcase
authorBio: Lee Child is an author whose bibliography includes The Enemy, One Shot, and Gone Tomorrow, spanning Mystery.

title: Isla and the Happily Ever After
author: Stephanie Perkins
synopsis: Love ignites in the City That Never Sleeps, but can it last? Hopeless romantic Isla has had a crush on introspective cartoonist Josh since their first year at the School of America in Paris.
authorBio: Stephanie Perkins is an author whose bibliography includes Anna and the French Kiss and Isla and the Happily Ever After, spanning Romance.

title: The Witching Hour
author: Anne Rice
synopsis: From the author of the extraordinary Vampire Chronicles comes a huge, hypnotic novel of witchcraft and the occult through four centuries.Demonstrating, once again, her gift for spellbinding storytelling and the creation of legend, Anne Rice makes real for us a great dynasty of witches-a family given to poetry and to incest, to murder and to philosophy; a family that, over the ages, is itself haunted by a powerful, dangerous, and seductive being.On the veranda of a great New Orleans house, now faded, a mute and...
authorBio: Anne Rice is an author whose bibliography includes Interview with the Vampire, The Vampire Lestat, and The Queen of the Damned, spanning Classics, Fantasy, and Sci-Fi.

title: The Complete Anne of Green Gables Boxed Set
author: L.M. Montgomery
synopsis: Favorites for nearly 100 years, these classic novels follow the adventures of the spirited redhead Anne Shirley, who comes to stay at Green Gables and wins the hearts of everyone she meets.Includes Anne of Green Gables, Anne of Avonlea, Anne of the Island, Anne of Windy Poplars, Anne's House of Dreams, Anne of Ingleside, Rainbow Valley and Rilla of Ingleside - the whole collection. Each book includes: The original, unabridged text; a specially commissioned biography of L.M.
authorBio: L.M. Montgomery is an author whose bibliography includes Anne of Avonlea, Anne of the Island, and The Complete Anne of Green Gables Boxed Set, spanning Children's.

title: Moneyball: The Art of Winning an Unfair Game
author: Michael Lewis
synopsis: Billy Beane, general manager of MLB's Oakland A's and protagonist of Michael Lewis's Moneyball, had a problem: how to win in the Major Leagues with a budget that's smaller than that of nearly every other team. Conventional wisdom long held that big name, highly athletic hitters and young pitchers with rocket arms were the ticket to success.
authorBio: Michael Lewis is an author whose bibliography includes The Big Short: Inside the Doomsday Machine, Moneyball: The Art of Winning an Unfair Game, and The Blind Side, spanning Non-Fiction.

title: Kane and Abel
author: Jeffrey Archer
synopsis: Born on the same day near the turn of the century on opposite sides of the world, both men are brought together by fate and the quest of a dream. These two men -- ambitious, powerful, ruthless -- are locked in a relentless struggle to build an empire, fuelled by their all-consuming hatred.
authorBio: Jeffrey Archer is an author whose bibliography includes Kane and Abel, Only Time Will Tell, and The Sins of the Father, spanning Mystery.

title: Changes
author: Jim Butcher
synopsis: Long ago, Susan Rodriguez was Harry Dresden's lover-until she was attacked by his enemies, leaving her torn between her own humanity and the bloodlust of the vampiric Red Court. Susan then disappeared to South America, where she could fight both her savage gift and those who cursed her with it.
authorBio: Jim Butcher is an author whose bibliography includes Grave Peril, Blood Rites, and Proven Guilty, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: The Grownup
author: Gillian Flynn
synopsis: A canny young woman is struggling to survive by perpetrating various levels of mostly harmless fraud. On a rainy April morning, she is reading auras at Spiritual Palms when Susan Burke walks in.
authorBio: Gillian Flynn is an author whose bibliography includes Dark Places and The Grownup, spanning Mystery.

title: Armada
author: Ernest Cline
synopsis: Zack Lightman has spent his life dreaming. Dreaming that the real world could be a little more like the countless science-fiction books, movies, and videogames he's spent his life consuming.
authorBio: Ernest Cline is an author whose bibliography includes Ready Player One and Armada, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Small Gods
author: Terry Pratchett
synopsis: Just because you can't explain it, doesn't mean it's a miracle.' Religion is a controversial business in the Discworld. Everyone has their own opinion, and indeed their own gods.
authorBio: Terry Pratchett is an author whose bibliography includes The Color of Magic, Equal Rites, and Small Gods, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: The A.B.C. Murders
author: Agatha Christie
synopsis: When Alice Asher is murdered in Andover, Hercule Poirot is already on to the clues. Alphabetically speaking, it's one down, twenty-five to go.There's a serial killer on the loose.
authorBio: Agatha Christie is an author whose bibliography includes The Mysterious Affair at Styles, Murder at the Vicarage, and Death on the Nile, spanning Mystery.

title: Prodigal Summer
author: Barbara Kingsolver
synopsis: Prodigal Summer weaves together three stories of human love within a larger tapestry of lives inhabiting the forested mountains and struggling small farms of southern Appalachia.From her outpost in an isolated mountain cabin, Deanna Wolfe, a reclusive wildlife biologist, watches a den of coyotes that have recently migrated into the region. She is caught off-guard by a young hunter who invades her most private spaces and confounds her self-assured, solitary life.
authorBio: Barbara Kingsolver is an author whose bibliography includes The Poisonwood Bible, The Bean Trees, and Prodigal Summer, spanning Classics, Fiction, and Romance.

title: Caliban's War
author: James S.A. Corey
synopsis: We are not alone.On Ganymede, breadbasket of the outer planets, a Martian marine watches as her platoon is slaughtered by a monstrous supersoldier. On Earth, a high-level politician struggles to prevent interplanetary war from reigniting.
authorBio: James S.A. Corey is an author whose bibliography includes Leviathan Wakes, Caliban's War, and Abaddon's Gate, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Shadowfever
author: Karen Marie Moning
synopsis: "Evil is a completely different creature, Mac. Evil is bad that believes it's good." - MacKayla Lane was just a child when she and her sister, Alina, were given up for adoption and banished from Ireland forever.
authorBio: Karen Marie Moning is an author whose bibliography includes Darkfever, Shadowfever, and Bloodfever, spanning Romance.

title: The Time Keeper
author: Mitch Albom
synopsis: In this fable, the first man on earth to count the hours becomes Father Time. The inventor of the world's first clock is punished for trying to measure God's greatest gift.
authorBio: Mitch Albom is an author whose bibliography includes Tuesdays with Morrie, The Five People You Meet in Heaven, and For One More Day, spanning Classics, Non-Fiction, Sci-Fi, and Self-Help.

title: Horton Hears a Who!
author: Dr. Seuss
synopsis: Academy Award winner Dustin Hoffman's masterful narration brings to life the heartwarming tale of Horton the elephant. Original music and sound effects complement the retelling.
authorBio: Dr. Seuss is an author whose bibliography includes How the Grinch Stole Christmas!, Oh, the Places You'll Go!, and The Lorax, spanning Children's.

title: The Iron Queen
author: Julie Kagawa
synopsis: My name is Meghan Chase.I thought it was over. That my time with the fey, the impossible choices I had to make, the sacrifices of those I loved, was behind me.
authorBio: Julie Kagawa is an author whose bibliography includes The Iron King, The Iron Daughter, and The Iron Queen, spanning Romance and Sci-Fi.

title: Children of the Mind
author: Orson Scott Card
synopsis: Children of the Mind (1996) is the fourth novel of Orson Scott Card's popular Ender's Game series of science fiction novels that focus on the character Ender Wiggin. This book was originally the second half of Xenocide, before it was split into two novels.At the start of Children of the Mind, Jane, the evolved computer intelligence, is using her newly discovered abilities to take the races of buggers, humans and pequeninos outside the universe and back instantaneously.
authorBio: Orson Scott Card is an author whose bibliography includes Speaker for the Dead, Ender's Shadow, and Children of the Mind, spanning Children's and Sci-Fi.

title: The Rise of Nine
author: Pittacus Lore
synopsis: The Rise of Nine is the next thrilling instalment in the gripping Lorien Legacies series by Pittacus Lore.'Number Four is a hero for this generation' Michael Bay, director of Transformers***Until I met John Smith, Number Four, I'd been on the run alone, hiding and fighting to stay alive. Together we are much more powerful.
authorBio: Pittacus Lore is an author whose bibliography includes I Am Number Four, The Power of Six, and The Rise of Nine, spanning Sci-Fi.
staffNote: A strong bookstore pick for readers of sci-fi.

title: Bone Crossed
author: Patricia Briggs

authorBio: Elizabeth Gilbert is an author whose bibliography includes Eat, Pray, Love, City of Girls, and Big Magic: Creative Living Beyond Fear, spanning Fiction, Romance, and Self-Help.

And sure enough, from the world he lives in-no phone, no address, no commitments-ex-military investigator Jack Reacher is coming. authorBio: Lee Child is an author whose bibliography includes The Enemy, One Shot, and Gone Tomorrow, spanning Mystery.

authorBio: Karen Marie Moning is an author whose bibliography includes Darkfever, Shadowfever, and Bloodfever, spanning Romance.

title: Silver Borne

author: David Baldacci

authorBio: David Baldacci is an author whose bibliography includes Memory Man, Absolute Power, and The Innocent, spanning Mystery.

author: Anthony Horowitz

But her secret is in constant danger of being discovered.With World War I brewing, Alek and Deryn's paths cross in the most unexpected way…taking them on a fantastical, around-the-world adventure that will change both
authorBio: Scott Westerfeld is an author whose bibliography includes Uglies, Pretties, and Specials, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: 2 States: The Story of My Marriage
author: Chetan Bhagat
synopsis: Love marriages around the world are simple: Boy loves girl. Girl loves boy. They get married. In India, there are a few more steps: Boy loves Girl. Girl loves Boy. They get married.Welcome to 2 States, a story about Krish and Ananya. They are from two different states of India, deeply in love and want to get married. Of course, their parent
authorBio: Chetan Bhagat is an author whose bibliography includes 2 States: The Story of My Marriage, Five Point Someone: What Not to Do at IIT, and The 3 Mistakes of My Life, spanning Romance.

title: Dry
author: Augusten Burroughs

If Death doesn't come for you, then what are you supposed to do in the meantime? You can't have the undead wandering about like lost souls. There's no telling what might happen, particularly when they discover that life really i
authorBio: Terry Pratchett is an author whose bibliography includes The Color of Magic, Equal Rites, and Small Gods, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Austenland
author: Shannon Hale
synopsis: Jane Hayes is a seemingly normal young New Yorker, but she has a secret. synopsis: Fighting terrorism on foreign ground, CIA superagent Mitch Rapp does whatever it takes to protect American freedom.CIA intelligence has pointed to a major terrorist attack on the United States, just as the nation's capital prepares for a grand Memorial Day tribute to the veterans of World War II. Racing to Afghanistan, Mitch Rapp leads a commando raid on an al Queda stronghold in a remote border village-and defuses plans for a nuclear strike on Washington.
authorBio: Vince Flynn is an author whose bibliography includes American Assassin, Extreme Measures, and Transfer of Power, spanning Mystery.

title: Fire and Ice
author: Erin Hunter
synopsis: Fireheart could hear a roaring around him, like wind in tall trees. The acrid stench of the Thunderpath stung his nostrils, together with a new smell, sharper and more terrifying.
authorBio: Erin Hunter is an author whose bibliography includes Fire and Ice, Forest of Secrets, and Rising Storm, spanning Children's.

title: Iron Gold
author: Pierce Brown
synopsis: They call him father, liberator, warlord, Reaper. But he feels a boy as he falls toward the pale blue planet, his armor red, his army vast, his heart heavy.
authorBio: Pierce Brown is an author whose bibliography includes Red Rising, Morning Star, and Iron Gold, spanning Sci-Fi.
staffNote: A strong bookstore pick for readers of sci-fi.

title: Possible Side Effects
author: Augusten Burroughs
synopsis: National Bestseller From the #1 New York Times bestselling author of Running with Scissors comes Augusten Burroughs's most provocative collection of true stories yet. authorBio: Augusten Burroughs is an author whose bibliography includes Running with Scissors, Dry, and Magical Thinking: True Stories, spanning Fantasy and Non-Fiction.

authorBio: Sherrilyn Kenyon is an author whose bibliography includes Night Pleasures, Acheron, and Seize the Night, spanning Romance.

title: The Fall of the House of Usher
author: Edgar Allan Poe
synopsis: Dive into this classic from the singular mind of Edgar Allan Poe, who is widely regarded as the master of short horror fiction. "The Fall of the House of Usher" recounts the terrible events that befall the last remaining members of the once-illustrious Usher clan before it is -- quite literally -- rent asunder.
authorBio: Edgar Allan Poe is an author whose bibliography includes The Complete Stories and Poems, The Cask of Amontillado, and The Pit and the Pendulum, spanning Mystery.

title: Tortilla Flat

At the center of the tale is Danny, whose house, like Arthur's castle, becomes a gathering place for men looking for adventure, camaraderie, and a...
authorBio: John Steinbeck is an author whose bibliography includes The Pearl, Cannery Row, and Travels with Charley: In Search of America, spanning Classics.
staffNote: A strong bookstore pick for readers of classics.

title: Then Came You
author: Jennifer Weiner

authorBio: Jennifer Weiner is an author whose bibliography includes Good in Bed, In Her Shoes, and Little Earthquakes, spanning Romance.
staffNote: A strong bookstore pick for readers of romance.

title: Missoula: Rape and the Justice System in a College Town
author: Jon Krakauer
synopsis: From bestselling author Jon Krakauer, a stark, powerful, meticulously reported narrative about a series of sexual assaults at the University of Montana ­- stories that illuminate the human drama behind the national plague of campus rape. Missoula, Montana, is a typical college town, with a highly regarded state university, bucolic surroundings, a lively social scene, and an excellent football team - the Grizzlies - with a rabid fan base.
authorBio: Jon Krakauer is an author whose bibliography includes Into the Wild, Under the Banner of Heaven, and Missoula: Rape and the Justice System in a College Town, spanning Classics, Mystery, and Non-Fiction.

title: Someone We Know
author: Shari Lapena
synopsis: Maybe you don't know your neighbors as well as you thought you did . . . "This is a very difficult letter to write. I hope you will not hate us too much. . . My son broke into your home recently while you were out." After two anonymous letters are received, whispers start to circulate,
authorBio: Shari Lapena is an author whose bibliography includes The Couple Next Door, A Stranger in the House, and An Unwanted Guest, spanning Mystery.

title: Remarkable Creatures
author: Tracy Chevalier

authorBio: Tracy Chevalier is an author whose bibliography includes Girl with a Pearl Earring, Remarkable Creatures, and The Lady and the Unicorn, spanning Classics, Mystery, and Romance.

authorBio: Karin Slaughter is an author whose bibliography includes Pretty Girls, Blindsighted, and Triptych, spanning Mystery.

authorBio: Neal Shusterman is an author whose bibliography includes Unwind, Thunderhead, and The Toll, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Touch of Power
author: Maria V. Snyder

author: Kathy Reichs

title: Juliet, Naked
author: Nick Hornby

authorBio: Nick Hornby is an author whose bibliography includes High Fidelity, A Long Way Down, and How to Be Good, spanning Classics and Romance.

authorBio: Sara Shepard is an author whose bibliography includes Pretty Little Liars, Flawless, and Unbelievable, spanning Mystery.

authorBio: Pittacus Lore is an author whose bibliography includes I Am Number Four, The Power of Six, and The Rise of Nine, spanning Sci-Fi.

staffNote: A strong bookstore pick for readers of mystery.

title: Bare Bones
author: Kathy Reichs
synopsis: It's a summer of sizzling heat in Charlotte where Dr. Temperance Brennan, forensic anthropologist for the North Carolina medical examiner, looks forward to her first vacation in years.
authorBio: Kathy Reichs is an author whose bibliography includes Déjà Dead, Fatal Voyage, and Death du Jour, spanning Mystery.

title: The Eye of Minds
author: James Dashner
synopsis: Michael is a gamer. And like most gamers, he almost spends more time on the VirtNet than in the actual world. The VirtNet offers total mind and body immersion, and it's addictive. Thanks to technology, anyone with enough money can experience fantasy worlds, risk their life without the chance of death, or just hang around with Virt-friends. And the more hacking skills you have, the more fun. Why bother following the rules when most of them are dumb, anyway?But some rules were made for a reason. Some technology is to

title: Mister Monday
author: Garth Nix
synopsis: Arthur Penhaligon's first days at his new school don't go too well, particularly when a fiendish Mister Monday appears, gives Arthur a magical clock hand, and then orders his gang of dog-faced goons to chase Arthur around and get it back. But when the confused and curious boy discovers that a mysterious virus is spreading through town, he decides to enter an otherworldly house to stop it.
authorBio: Garth Nix is an author whose bibliography includes Abhorsen, Lirael, and Mister Monday, spanning Children's and Sci-Fi.

title: Truth and Beauty
author: Ann Patchett
synopsis: Ann Patchett and the late Lucy Grealy met in college in 1981, and, after enrolling in the Iowa Writers' Workshop, began a friendship that would be as defining to both of their lives as their work. In Grealy's critically acclaimed memoir Autobiography of a Face, she wrote about losing part of her jaw to childhood cancer, years of chemotherapy and radiation, and endless reconstructive surgeries.
authorBio: Ann Patchett is an author whose bibliography includes Bel Canto, State of Wonder, and Run, spanning Classics, Fiction, Mystery, Non-Fiction, and Romance.

title: Darker
author: E.L. James
synopsis: E L James revisits the world of Fifty Shades with a deeper and darker take on the love story that has enthralled millions of readers around the globe. Their scorching, sensual affair ended in heartbreak and recrimination, but Christian Grey cannot get Anastasia Steele out of his mind, or his blood.
authorBio: E.L. James is an author whose bibliography includes Fifty Shades of Grey, Fifty Shades Darker, and Fifty Shades Freed, spanning Romance.

title: The Complete Calvin and Hobbes
author: Bill Watterson
synopsis: [ Box Set | Book One | Book Two | Book Three ]Calvin and Hobbes is unquestionably one of the most popular comic strips of all time. The imaginative world of a boy and his real-only-to-him tiger was first syndicated in 1985 and appeared in more than 2,400 newspapers when Bill Watterson retired on January 1, 1996.
authorBio: Bill Watterson is an author whose bibliography includes The Essential Calvin and Hobbes: A Calvin and Hobbes Treasury, The Calvin and Hobbes Tenth Anniversary Book, and The Complete Calvin and Hobbes, spanning Children's.

title: Rage of Angels
author: Sidney Sheldon
synopsis: A worldwide bestseller first published in 1980, this novel tells the story of Jennifer Parker, a successful lawyer who is loved by two men, one a politician, the other, a mafia don.
authorBio: Sidney Sheldon is an author whose bibliography includes If Tomorrow Comes, Master of the Game, and Tell Me Your Dreams, spanning Mystery.

title: The Selection Stories: The Prince & The Guard
author: Kiera Cass
synopsis: Two novellas set in the world of Kiera Cass's #1 New York Times bestselling Selection series are now available in print for the first time. The Prince and The Guard both offer captivating views into the hearts and minds of the two men fighting to win America Singer's love.
authorBio: Kiera Cass is an author whose bibliography includes The Selection, The Elite, and The One, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy: A Trilogy in Four Parts
author: Douglas Adams
synopsis: Charting the whole of Arthur Dent's odyssey through space are:THE HITCHHIKER'S GUIDE TO THE GALAXY.One Thursday lunchtime the Earth gets unexpectedly demolished to make way for a new hyperspace bypass. For Arthur Dent, who has only just had his house demolished that morning, this seems already to be more than he can cope with.
authorBio: Douglas Adams is an author whose bibliography includes The Ultimate Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Life, the Universe and Everything, and Mostly Harmless, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Dragonsdawn
author: Anne McCaffrey
synopsis: The beautiful planet Pern seemed a paradise to its new colonists - until unimaginable terror turned it into hell. Suddenly deadly spores were falling like silver threads from the sky, devouring everything - and everyone - in their path.
authorBio: Anne McCaffrey is an author whose bibliography includes Dragonflight, Dragonsong, and Dragonsinger, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Industrial Magic
author: Kelley Armstrong
synopsis: Meet the smart, sexy - supernatural - women of the otherworld. This is not your mother's coven... Kelley Armstrong returns with the eagerly awaited follow-up to Dime Store Magic. Paige Winterbourne, a headstrong young woman haunted by a dark legacy, is now put to the ultimate test as she fights to save innocents from the most insidious evil of all.. . . In the aftermath of her mother's murder, Paige broke with the elite, ultraconservative American Coven of Witches. Now her goal is to start a new Coven for a new gen
authorBio: Kelley Armstrong is an author whose bibliography includes The Summoning, The Gathering, and Industrial Magic, spanning Romance.

title: Magic Kingdom for Sale/Sold
author: Terry Brooks
synopsis: Landover was a genuine magic kingdom, complete with fairy folk and wizardry, just as the advertisement had promised. But after he purchased it for a million dollars, Ben Holiday discovered that there were a few details the ad had failed to mention.
authorBio: Terry Brooks is an author whose bibliography includes The Sword of Shannara, The Wishsong of Shannara, and The Talismans of Shannara, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Fever Pitch
author: Nick Hornby

And that's before the players even take the field.Nick Hornby has been a football fan since the moment he was conceived. Call it predestiny. Or call it preschool. Fever Pitch is his tribute to a lifelong obsession. authorBio: Nick Hornby is an author whose bibliography includes High Fidelity, A Long Way Down, and How to Be Good, spanning Classics and Romance.

title: Tricks
author: Ellen Hopkins
synopsis: Five teenagers from different parts of the country. Three girls. Two guys. Four straight. One gay. Some rich. Some poor. Some from great families. Some with no one at all. All living their lives as best they can, but all searching ... for freedom, safety, community, family, love. What they don't expect, though, is all that can happen when those powerful little words "I love you" are said for all the wrong reasons.Five moving stories remain separate at first, then interweave to tell a larger, powerful story-a story
authorBio: Ellen Hopkins is an author whose bibliography includes Crank, Impulse, and Glass, spanning Romance.

title: One Good Turn
author: Kate Atkinson
synopsis: It is summer, it is the Edinburgh Festival. People queuing for a lunchtime show witness a road-rage incident - a near-homicidal attack which changes the lives of everyone involved.
authorBio: Kate Atkinson is an author whose bibliography includes Life After Life, Case Histories, and When Will There Be Good News?, spanning Fantasy and Mystery.

title: The Book of Tomorrow
author: Cecelia Ahern
synopsis: Tamara Goodwin has always lived in the here and now, never giving a second thought to tomorrow. authorBio: Cecelia Ahern is an author whose bibliography includes P.S. I Love You, Love, Rosie, and Thanks for the Memories, spanning Mystery and Romance.

title: Sisterhood Everlasting
author: Ann Brashares
synopsis: From #1 New York Times bestselling author Ann Brashares comes the welcome return of the characters whose friendship became a touchstone for a generation. Now Tibby, Lena, Carmen, and Bridget have grown up, starting their lives on their own.
authorBio: Ann Brashares is an author whose bibliography includes The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants, The Second Summer of the Sisterhood, and Girls in Pants: The Third Summer of the Sisterhood, spanning Children's and Romance.

title: Conspiracy in Death

authorBio: J.D. Robb is an author whose bibliography includes Immortal in Death, Ceremony in Death, and Vengeance in Death, spanning Sci-Fi.

title: Dime Store Magic
author: Kelley Armstrong
synopsis: Paige Winterbourne was always either too young or too rebellious to succeed her mother as leader of one of the world's most powerful elite organizations- the American Coven of Witches. Now that she is twenty-three and her mother is dead, the Elders can no longer deny her.
authorBio: Kelley Armstrong is an author whose bibliography includes The Summoning, The Gathering, and Industrial Magic, spanning Romance.

title: River Secrets

authorBio: Shannon Hale is an author whose bibliography includes The Goose Girl, Princess Academy, and Austenland, spanning Children's and Romance.

title: Just Ella

synopsis: Being a princess isn't all that...You've heard the fairy tale: a glass slipper, Prince Charming, happily ever after... authorBio: Margaret Peterson Haddix is an author whose bibliography includes Among the Hidden, Into the Gauntlet, and Found, spanning Children's.

title: The Fever Code

synopsis: Once there was a world's end.The forests burned, the lakes and rivers dried up, and the oceans swelled.Then came a plague, and fever spread across the globe. Families died, violence reigned, and man killed man.Next came WICKED, who were looking for an answer.

staffNote: A strong bookstore pick for readers of sci-fi.

title: A Spot of Bother

authorBio: Mark Haddon is an author whose bibliography includes The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time and A Spot of Bother, spanning Classics and Mystery.

title: Love Anthony

title: Eragon, Eldest & Brisingr

title: Where Men Win Glory: The Odyssey of Pat Tillman

Alia Keralis just wanted to escape her overprotective brother with a semester at sea. She doesn't know she is being hunted by people who think her v

title: A Man Named Dave

authorBio: Dave Pelzer is an author whose bibliography includes A Child Called "It", The Lost Boy, and A Man Named Dave, spanning Mystery and Non-Fiction.

title: Angels and Demons / The Da Vinci Code (Robert Langdon, #1-2)
